newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Profit-takers lurk on European bourses.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Profit-takers lurk on European bourses.

text.p: European share markets were mostly weaker on Friday as investors cashed in on this week's record run for a second day, but London rose modestly mainly for technical reasons.

Expiry of options contracts influenced both the London and Frankfurt markets, albeit in opposite directions, while Paris suffered from worries that the new Socialist government would raise taxes to tackle the budget deficit.
The dollar held stable on the foreign exchange markets.
Paris suffered the most among the leading European bourses with the CAC-40 down 32.93 points or 1.11 percent at 2,925.66 by mid morning.

A French government source said ministers were studying a possible increase in corporate tax and raising company social security contributions to cut the budget deficit, which is expected to be around 3.6 percent of gross domestic product -- well above the 3.0 percent target for joining the single European currency.

But shares in Club Mditerrane jumped on news that the Trigano family, which founded the leisure empire, had quit the supervisory board. They were up 4.17 percent even though the company, now run by the former boss of the Euro Disney theme park, reported a 413 million franc ($68.2 million) first-half loss.
German shares, which closed at a record high on Thursday, also suffered. The DAX index of blue chips was down 34.49 points or 0.82 percent at 4,192.82.

"I think the market looks a bit tired," said one Frankfurt dealer. "We could fall rather quickly today like we did on Thursday for no apparent reason. The market needs to take a rest before moving higher."

Dealers blamed some of the losses on the expiry of the DAX options due to signs of heavy open interest at 4,200 points. Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial average closed down 18.11 points at 8,020.77 overnight, also weighed on sentiment.
Some traders looked for the DAX to find support at about 4,155 to 4,160 points, saying the losses would help the market to make further gains and reach new records.
London went against the trend, with the FTSE-100 index climbing back into record territory. By midmorning it was up 41.8 points or 0.84 percent at 4,990.8.
But dealers said it was being dragged up by the expiry of July options, rather than any renewal of the feverish buying seen earlier in the week.
"Friday is never a great day to start a new initiative," said one equity salesman. "Most people may be quite prepared just to keep their heads down."

The market also failed to react to M4 money supply figures even though the strong data reinforced expectations that British interest rates have to rise. London's bull run increasingly seems to defy economic logic but so far it shows no signs of ending for good.
On the foreign exchanges the dollar was steady above 1.79 marks, ignoring a survey from Germany's Ifo institute which showed the business climate was better in June than the market had expected.
The dollar was at 1.7932 marks compared with 1.7998 at the European close on Thursday.

It was also at 115.60 yen, down from 116.07 on Thursday. This followed the annual report from the Japanese Economic Planning Agency (EPA), which said the country's economic recovery was close to self-sustaining.

"The EPA annual report was upbeat and the market has picked up on the comments that companies and individuals need to be aware of interest rates rising," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International in London.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was at 115.60 yen and 1.7932 marks compared with 116.07 yen and 1.7998 marks in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 41.8 points or 0.84 percent at 4,990.8.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index of floor trade was down 34.49 points or 0.82 percent at 4,192.82.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 32.93 points or 1.11 percent at 2,925.66.
PRECIOUS METALS at 0900 GMT
Gold was at $323.50 an ounce compared with Thursday's European close of $319.55. Silver was six cents higher at $4.27. ($ = 6.056 French Francs)
